title: 2026 crematoria monitoring and emission-limit QA controls

sources.publisher: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
sources.title: Crematoria: emissions limits, monitoring and other provisions

sources.publisher: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
sources.title: Crematoria: process guidance note

facts.source_fact: The guidance identifies combustion temperature, secondary-chamber residence time, carbon monoxide and excess oxygen as key combustion controls.
facts.expected_handling: Require these operating-control fields where crematoria compliance is assessed.

facts.source_fact: Secondary-chamber residence time must be demonstrated by design calculation and verified at commissioning.
facts.expected_handling: Do not accept design-only residence-time evidence when commissioning verification is required.

facts.source_fact: Relevant substances in the monitoring tables must be controlled and monitored.
facts.expected_handling: Map each monitored substance to the applicable table and permit condition.

facts.source_fact: Emissions monitoring must use the specified standard or an equivalent method agreed by the regulator.
facts.expected_handling: Reject undocumented substitute methods.

facts.source_fact: Even where no emission limit applies to NOx or mercury from unabated cremators, operators must measure and report them and provide data for review purposes.
facts.expected_handling: Do not equate absence of an ELV with absence of monitoring duties.

facts.source_fact: The guidance warns that referenced BS, CEN and ISO standards are periodically amended and updated.
facts.expected_handling: Verify the current standard version before accepting a monitoring method.

facts.source_fact: Calibration must be carried out before measurements using relevant methods at least annually and results reported to the regulator.
facts.expected_handling: Require a valid calibration date and regulator-reporting evidence.

facts.source_fact: Crematoria with flue-gas treatment must have a continuously operating dust-arrestment plant monitor to detect failures likely to cause particulate ELV exceedance.
facts.expected_handling: Require continuous monitor status for flue-gas-treatment configurations.

facts.source_fact: The guidance states all activities must comply with emission limits in Tables 5 and 6.
facts.expected_handling: Apply the correct table by cremator configuration and status.

facts.source_fact: Emission-limit reference conditions are 273.1 K, 101.3 kPa, 11% oxygen by volume and dry gas unless otherwise stated.
facts.expected_handling: Normalize measurements to the stated reference conditions before ELV comparison.

facts.source_fact: Compliance is generally assessed using an average of three consecutive 60-minute measurements unless otherwise stated.
facts.expected_handling: Do not compare a non-equivalent averaging period to the ELV.

facts.source_fact: Monitoring should start once stable airflow is established, typically about two minutes after cremation starts, and continue for one hour.
facts.expected_handling: Validate the monitoring window against the process timing rule.

facts.source_fact: The guidance defines conditions that invalidate tests and require them to be repeated.
facts.expected_handling: Flag invalid-run conditions and exclude those measurements from compliance evidence.

facts.source_fact: For unabated cremators particulate matter is limited to 80 mg/Nm3 or 120 g over the stated cremation monitoring period.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve whether the permit applies concentration or mass form.

facts.source_fact: For unabated cremators hydrogen chloride is limited to 60 mg/Nm3 or 100 g over the stated period.
facts.expected_handling: Preserve the permit-selected concentration or mass basis.

facts.source_fact: For unabated cremators total organic carbon has a 20 mg/Nm3 concentration limit.
facts.expected_handling: Apply the correct TOC averaging period and configuration.

facts.source_fact: New cremators have tighter particulate, HCl and TOC limits than existing cremators in Table 6.
facts.expected_handling: Require existing/new status before selecting an ELV.

facts.source_fact: Table 6 specifies a 200 mg/Nm3 NOx limit for all cremators from four years after publication.
facts.expected_handling: Apply the implementation date before enforcing this future-dated limit.

facts.source_fact: Table 6 specifies mercury limits of 50 µg/Nm3 for existing and 30 µg/Nm3 for new cremators, and PCDD/F at 0.1 ng/Nm3 for all.
facts.expected_handling: Select mercury limit by installation status and preserve PCDD/F units.

facts.source_fact: The guidance uses short-term process contribution below 10% and long-term contribution below 1% of the environmental standard as screening criteria before detailed assessment.
facts.expected_handling: Require both screening criteria before concluding no further air-quality assessment is needed.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve the cited source fact without broadening its scope.
Attach the applicable accounting, monitoring or regulatory boundary before downstream use.
Attach reference year, publication/update date and provisional/final status where applicable.
Carry source URL, publisher and method/provenance into derived outputs.
Do not convert this method or regulatory rule into a parcel-level measured emission without a separate parcel-binding gate.

generation_rule: CARTESIAN_PRODUCT facts x guard_patterns; control_id={package_id}_{fact_id}_{pattern_id}; each generated row inherits confidence_percent=99 and verification=PASS
